The drawback of our plan to exchange bishops is that Black can occupy the center.

Let's trade on d5.

rnb1k2r/pp2q1pp/2p5/3npp2/8/NP2PN2/P2PBP.text:
Black will probably recapture with the knight.

To untangle our pieces, we'll have to move the knight first.

Although it looks passive, I suggest retreating to b1.

rnb2r1k/pp2q1pp/2p5/3npp2/2B5/1P2PN2/P2P.text:
The most logical is for Black to slide the king to h8.

And we'll actually trade on d5 as well.

rnb2r1k/pp2q1pp/8/3ppp2/8/1P2PN2/P2P1PPP.text:
After Black captures, here is our point.

We'll try to trade the queens, just as we've tried to trade the bishops!

The point is to weaken the dark squares yet again.

rnb2r1k/pp4pp/8/3ppp2/8/qP2PN2/P2P1PPP/R.text:
Black doesn't have much of a better move than to capture at this point.

We'll recapture. Now the e5-square is vulnerable and Black has got some loose pawns in the center, although they control it.

rnb2rk1/pp2q1pp/2p5/3npp2/8/1P2PN2/P2PBP.text:
Once Black castles, we can throw in a pin.

We'll bring our bishop to c4.

rnbq1rk1/pp4pp/2p1pn2/3p1p2/2PP4/NP2PN2/.text:
After recapturing, we've got strong control of e5 once again.

After we get the a3-knight to d3, our position will be comfortable to play.

rnbq1rk1/pp4pp/2pbpn2/3p1p2/2P5/BP2PN2/P.text:
Castling only avoids the trade for one move.

Now we finally get a pawn to d4!

Now Black won't be able to push ...e5 and their bishop will remain stuck for a while.

rnbqk2r/pp4pp/2p1pn2/3p1p2/2P5/bP2PN2/P2.text:
Black could also capture on a3.

We'll take with the knight, of course...

rnbqk2r/pp4pp/2pbpn2/3p1p2/2P5/1P2PN2/P2.text:
Having placed the pawns on the light squares, it's logical for Black to make the dark-squared bishop as active as possible.

That's why we'll try to trade it immediately!

Trading off the bishops is highly desirable for us as we can invade the central e5 square after.

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/8/2B5/4PN2/PP1P1P.text: Black might go for the standard ...Nf6...

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/2p2n2/8/2BP4/4PN2/PP3PP.text:
Which lets us play d4 with great control of the center, too.

You've got nothing to worry about in this position with a slight advantage already in the first five moves.

rnbqkb1r/pp4pp/2p1pn2/3p1p2/2P5/1P2PN2/P.text:
Black goes for ...Nf6 now, a standard developing move on the kingside.

Let's get our king to safety.

rnbqkbnr/pp1ppppp/2p5/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R.text:
Black will play ...c6 to prepare ...d5, as per usual.

We'll get the knight out with the idea of e3 to protect c4.

rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/3p4/2P5/5N2/PP1PPPP.text:
And Black should play ...d5, after all.

Let's defend the pawn with e3, as we can't play e4.

Now our light-squared bishop is ready to get into the action.

rnbqkbnr/pp2pppp/2p5/8/2p5/4PN2/PP1P1PPP.text:
Black can capture on c4 at
various points, perhaps mistakenly thinking they are in a Queen's Gambit Accepted position. 

This move is played only 9% of the time in this position, however.

We'll just recapture on c4. Our kingside is already developed.

rnbqkbnr/pp3ppp/2p1p3/3p4/2P5/4PN2/PP1P1.text:
3...e6 is the third most popular move in this position, with a popularity of 13%.

Black might be going for a Stonewall structure!

The Stonewall is a popular and aggressive option but not without flaws - principally the bad bishop on c8 and potential dark square weaknesses. 

Our task will be to exploit these drawbacks, starting with b3 to play Bb2 or Ba3.

rnbqkbnr/pp4pp/2p1p3/3p1p2/2P5/1P2PN2/P2.text:
Black expands with ...f5 now.

This move signifies the Stonewall.

Their idea will be to get the knight to f6 and often to e4 at some point.

We'll simply continue developing and prepare castling.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In the third and last study of sidelines, we'll see what to play against the Stonewall and other lines that Black may play.

We'll go for the English with 1.c4.

r1b1k2r/pp2pp1p/2n2bpP/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PPK.text:
Our king finds a safe square on c2.

The plan is to expand on the queenside and develop the bishop. 

The c3-pawn nicely restricts Black's knight.

r1bqk2r/ppp1ppbp/2n3p1/3n3P/8/2N2N2/PP1P.text:
Continuing development here happens in 10% of the games. 

It is best for Black: they can even castle queenside in some cases.

We'll push in the center here. Another promising path is 7. g3.

r1bqr1k1/ppp2pb1/2n3p1/3np1N1/8/2N1P1Q1/.text:
We do as well.

The plan is to bring the bishop to c4 from where it will join the attack.

r2q1rk1/ppp1pp1p/2n2bpP/3n4/3P2b1/2N1PN2.text:
Black hides their king.

We'll prepare to castle and break the pin.

r2q1rk1/ppp2p1p/2n2bpP/3np3/3P2b1/2N1PN2.text:
...e5 is a great move here.  

Black needs to fight back before we fully develop.

We'll trade on d5, forcing a slightly better endgame. 

11. Nxe5 was also possible with a similar concept.

r2qk2r/pp1bppbp/2n3p1/2p4P/5Q2/2P2N2/P2P.text:
Black develops.

Now e4 is a nice move to expand in the center. 

The queen is well-placed to defend
the center and put pressure on Black's kingside.

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n2b2/5p1P/3PP3/2P2N2/P4.text:
Black wants to isolate our f5-pawn if we recapture...

...so we expand in the center instead!

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n2bp1/3n1P1P/3P4/2N2N2/.text:
Black retreats the bishop.

We'll expand in the center with a tempo.

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n2bp1/3n1b1P/3P3R/2N2N2.text:
Black attacks our rook.

We don't care! 

We ignore the threat of material loss and expand on the kingside instead.

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n2bpP/3n4/3P2b1/2N2N2/P.text:
Black saves the bishop.

White are looking to continue solid development with a space advantage, and we'll play e3.

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n3p1/3n1b1P/3P2Pb/2N2N2.text:
Black accepts the sacrifice.

We'll go with the capture on f5.

r2qk2r/ppp1pp1p/2n5/4bp1P/3P4/2P2N2/P4P2.text:
Black must give up the bishop, otherwise their position will collapse with our advancing pawns coming.

We'll recapture with the pawn.

r2qk2r/ppp1ppbp/2n3p1/3n1b1P/3P4/2N2N2/P.text:
Black is fighting against our e4 push.

But, with Rh4, we have an awesome rook lift to prepare e4!

This is a deep concept as it involves an exchange sacrifice.

r2qk2r/ppp1ppbp/2n3p1/3n3P/3P2b1/2N2N2/P.text:
Black might be tempted to attack our h5-pawn here.

The h-pawn isn't just a battering ram to open the position, but also a long-term strategic asset to cramp Black's kingside when pushed to h6.

r2qk2r/ppp1ppbp/2n5/4Pp1P/3P4/2P2N2/P4P2.text:
If Black retreats...

... the move h6 will come next! Attacking the bishop yet again.

r2qk2r/ppp2p1p/2n1p1p1/3n1P1P/3P3b/2N2N2.text:
The idea is to solidify the pawn structure on the kingside and protect the bishop on h4.

White should trade on e6 and isolate the pawn.

r2qk2r/ppp4p/2n1p1p1/3n3P/3P3b/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Black recaptures.

We develop the bishop to h3 and put pressure on the e6-pawn.

r2qkb1r/ppp1pp1p/2n4P/4Pp2/3P4/2P2N2/P4P.text:
The only free square.

We'll expand even further!

r2r2k1/ppp2p1p/4b1pP/4n3/8/1P2PP2/P5P1/R.text:
We'll castle here. 

Black is more active for the moment, but the bishop pair and cramping pawn structure on the kingside leave us optimistic.

r3k2r/pp1bppbp/2nq2p1/2p4P/2B1P3/2P1QN2/.text:
We'll continue our development. 

We keep the attacking opportunities on the kingside, and Ba3 to pressure the c5-pawn is a nice idea.

r3k2r/ppp1pp1p/2n5/4Pp1P/8/2P2N2/P4P2/R1.text:
And the two bishop endgame with a pawn up gives White a lot of winning chances.

Check out the game between GM Anish Giri and GM Peter Svidler in the chess24.com INT 2020.

r3k2r/ppp1q2p/2n1p1p1/3n3P/3P3b/2N2N1B/P.text:
The queen defends it.

We will trade off Black's active knight on d5.

r3k2r/ppp1q2p/2n3p1/3p3P/3P3b/5N1B/PP2PP.text:
Black recaptures.

With our next move of Bh6, the bishop is nicely eyeing the weak kingside dark squares.

r4rk1/ppp2p1p/2n2bpP/3qp3/3P2b1/4PN2/PP2.text:
The queen recaptures.

We'll capture on e5.

r4rk1/ppp2p1p/2n2bpP/4P3/6b1/4PN2/PP2BPP.text:
Black trades the queens.

We'll recapture with the bishop.

r4rk1/ppp2p1p/2n3pP/4b3/6b1/4PN2/PP3PP1/.text:
Black grabs the pawn on e5.

Let's trade yet again.

r4rk1/ppp2p1p/4b1pP/4n3/8/4PP2/PP4P1/R1B.text:
The bishop retreats to e6.

We'll play b3, with the idea that the dark-squared bishop might be developed to the a1-h8 diagonal later.

r4rk1/ppp2p1p/6pP/4n3/6b1/4P3/PP3PP1/R1B.text:
Black recaptures.

Instead of trading yet again, we'll harass the bishop with f3.

r6r/ppp1qk1p/2n3pB/3p3P/3P3b/4PN1B/PP3P2.text:
And we solidify the center. 

The position is complex but despite Black's extra exchange White has full compensation due to the bishop pair and general piece activity.

r6r/ppp1qk1p/2n3pB/3p3P/3P3b/5N1B/PP2PP2.text: Black cannot castle queenside, so they get their king out of the center via f7.

rn1qk2r/pp1bppbp/6p1/2p4P/Q7/2P2N2/P2PPP.text:
Black attacks our queen in return.

The queen is safe on f4 while remaining active.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pp1p/7P/3PPpN1/8/2P5/P4P2/R.text: This position is just crushing, with e6 and Qh5 coming.

rnb1k2r/pp2pp1p/5bpP/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PP3PP.text:
Black trades the queens.

We recapture.

rnb1r1k1/ppp2pb1/3q2p1/4p3/4P2Q/5N2/PP1P.text:
If Black goes to the d6-square...

...We'll expand in the center!

rnb1r1k1/ppp2pb1/3q2p1/8/3pP2Q/5N2/PP3PP.text: And after Black captures the "free" pawn...

rnb1r1k1/ppp2pb1/6p1/3qp3/7Q/5N2/PP1PPPP.text:
Black centralizes the rook and frees up the f8-square for their king.

We'll push e4, attacking the enemy queen and gaining space in the center at the same time. 

This move also prevents Black from pushing ...e4.

rnb2rk1/ppp2pb1/6p1/3qp3/Q7/5N2/PP1PPPP1.text:
The queen must recapture.

And now we are able to invade the h-file!

rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppb1/6p1/3n4/8/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
Black recaptures.

Qa4 is a clever and ambitious move, as we go for mate with the hidden idea of swinging the queen over to the kingside!

rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/6p1/3n3P/8/2N2N2/PP1PP.text:
6... O-O might also occur here, featuring in 15% of the games played, but it is not very wise.

We'll open up the h-file.

rnbq1rk1/ppp2pb1/4p1p1/3n4/Q7/2N2N2/PP1P.text:
Black covers the h4-square by pushing their pawn to e6.

So we'll go to g4 instead, and threaten Qh3!

rnbq1rk1/ppp2pb1/6p1/3np3/6Q1/2N2N2/PP1P.text:
Black is fighting to prevent an h-file invasion.

We'll retreat the queen to g3.

rnbq1rk1/ppp2pb1/6p1/3np3/Q7/2N2N2/PP1PP.text:
Black plays ...e5 immediately, again with the idea of preventing the queen's access to the h-file.

Let's trade the knights.

rnbqk2r/pp2pp1p/5bpP/2p5/4P3/2n2N2/PP1P1.text:
Black doesn't want to be passive, so they trade.

We'll recapture with the d-pawn! 

The endgame is very pleasant
with Black's pawn on c5 being weak and the bishop on f6 being short of squares.

rnbqk2r/pp2pp1p/5bpP/2pn4/8/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
The bishop escapes.

But we'll expand in the center with a tempo.

rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/6p1/2p4P/8/2P2N2/P2PPPP1.text:
Black controls the d4-square.

We'll give a check on a4. It's a clever way to activate our queen.

A good alternative was 8. g3 to
continue developing.

rnbqk2r/pp2ppbp/6p1/2pn3P/8/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
With 6...c5, which happens in 11% 
of the games, Black tries to get more central control. 

We can, however, clamp them on the kingside now with h6!

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/6p1/3n4/7P/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
Black ignores our attack and develops the bishop to g7.

We continue with our h-file assault, keeping the options for both
hxg6 and h6 to cramp Black further!

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppbp/6p1/7P/8/2n2N2/PP1PPPP1.text:
Black continues with the most popular move with 31% of games played — trading immediately on c3.

We'll recapture with the b-pawn.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/3n4/8/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
Black prepares to fianchetto.

We'll advance with h4.

The idea is to push h5 and attack the pawn structure.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p4/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP.text:
And here comes the move we are interested in. 

The early d5-push by Black immediately establishes a pawn in the center. 

We'll trade, otherwise ...d4 could come and Black will gain the desired central space!

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3n4/8/2N5/PP1PPPPP/R.text:
Black recaptures.

And we develop the knight.

rnbqkb1r/pppppppp/5n2/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R.text:
Black begins with the knight development.

We'll bring the knight to c3.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
For Chapter 6, we will see the Grunfeld. 

This is characterized by the early ...d5-push and the fianchetto on g7.

Let's begin with the English as always.

rnbqr1k1/ppp2pb1/6p1/3np3/8/2N2NQ1/PP1PP.text:
Black centralizes their rook.

Let's bring another piece to the kingside attack with Ng5!

rnbqr1k1/ppp2pb1/6p1/4p3/4P2Q/5N2/PP1P1P.text:
Black offers a queen trade, which would get them out of trouble.

We don't trade of course, but give a check on h7 instead.

rnbqrk2/ppp2pbQ/6p1/4p3/3PP3/5N2/PP3PP1/.text:
d4 is a very powerful move here. 

The bishop will invade via the h6 square and Black will have a hard time surviving.

rq2k2r/pp1bppbp/2n3p1/2p4P/4PQ2/2P2N2/P2.text:
A queen trade would help Black...

...so we'll decline it.

r1bq1rk1/p3pp2/1p4pp/2pP4/4P2P/8/PQ2BPP1.text:
The rook will get centralized to d1.

For the cost of a pawn we have good central control and very active pieces.

r1bq1rk1/pp2ppb1/2n3p1/2p3Np/4P2P/2P5/P2.text:
Let's activate the knight! 

Now we really see the benefit of including h4/h5 as we have great attacking chances on the kingside.

r1bq3r/pp2pk2/5pp1/3PP2p/2BQ3P/8/P2B1PP1.text:
But Bc4 seals the deal.

Black will not survive this attack.

r1bq3r/pp2pk2/5pp1/3PP2p/3Q3P/8/P2BBPP1/.text: Black tries to keep the position closed...

r1bq3r/pp2pk2/5ppp/3P4/3QP2P/8/P2BBPP1/5.text:
Black brings their king to a safer square.

We'll blast open the center!

r1bqk2r/p3pp2/1p4pp/2pP4/4P2P/1Q6/Pb2BPP.text:
Black trades.

We'll recapture with an attack on the rook.

r1bqk2r/p3pp2/1p4pp/2pP4/4P2P/2b5/P3BPP1.text:
Black secures the b-pawn.

Our queen comes to the queenside to eye some light squares and allow the rooks to be connected.

r1bqk2r/p3ppb1/1p4pp/2pP4/4P2P/1Q6/P3BPP.text:
The bishop retreats.

We'll offer to trade the dark-squared bishop.

It is Black's only good piece, so trading it off is a great idea here.

r1bqk2r/pp2p3/5ppp/3P4/3QP2P/8/P2BBPP1/4.text:
Black defends the rook.

We get castled.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/2n3pp/2pP4/4P2P/2b2N2/P3B.text:
Black accepts our sacrifice.

We'll block the check with the bishop.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/2n3pp/2pP4/4P2P/5N2/P2BBP.text:
Black goes for the material, and captures the rook.

But now our queen will be on a very powerful dark-squared diagonal. 

Both the knight and the rook are hanging.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/6pp/2pP4/3nP2P/5N2/P2BBPP.text:
The only move to defend both.

Let's get rid of the knight.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/6pp/2pP4/4P2P/2b5/P3BPP1/.text:
Black accepts it.

Our rook will occupy the semi-open b-file. 

Black is suffering, despite the extra pawn, due to the lack of development and central control.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/6pp/2pPb3/4P2P/2P5/P3BPP1.text:
Black recaptures.

We can safely castle here and offer the c3-pawn.

r1bqk2r/pp2pp2/6pp/3P4/3pP2P/8/P2BBPP1/Q.text:
Recapturing.

The queen captures on d4.

We're not even down significant material as we have the bishop pair and a pawn for the exchange.

r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2n3p1/2p4p/4P2P/2P2N2/P2.text:
Black continues with their development.

We'll place the rook on the semi-open b-file.

r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/2n3pp/2p5/3PP2P/2P2N2/P3.text:
Black continues with the development and puts pressure on the d4-pawn.

We'll push the d-pawn! 

This is a very standard anti-Grunfeld idea as we bulldoze Black in the center regardless of material investment!

r1bqk2r/pp2ppb1/6pp/2pPn3/4P2P/2P2N2/P3B.text:
Black decides not to go for the exchange and centralizes the knight instead.

We'll trade.

r2qk2r/ppp1ppb1/1nn3p1/7p/3PP2P/2N1BP2/P.text:
The king will be safe on the queenside. 

We have the bishop pair, so we'll open up the position with an f4-f5 advance.

rn1q1rk1/p3pp2/1p4p1/2pP3p/4PBbP/2b2N2/P.text: This might look like a free pawn for Black...

rn1q1rk1/p3pp2/1p4p1/2pPP2p/5BbP/2b2N2/P.text:
...but we cut off Black's bishop with e5.

Suddenly, the king lacks a defender.

rn1q1rk1/p3ppb1/1p4p1/2p4p/3PPBbP/2P2N2/.text:
Black advances the h-pawn to keep it safe.

We can now advance in the center with the typical d5!

rn1q1rk1/p3ppb1/1p4pp/2p5/3PP1bP/2P2N2/P.text:
Black protects their b-pawn.

Our dark-squared bishop will go to f4 and with Qd2 coming we prepare to pur pressure on the h6-pawn.

rn1q1rk1/pp2ppb1/6pp/2p5/3PP1bP/2P2N2/P3.text:
Black develops the bishop.

We'll occupy the semi-open b-file.

rn1qk2r/ppp1ppb1/1n4p1/7p/3PP1bP/2N1BN2/.text:
Black's bishop invades the g4-square and pins our knight.

We will simply get out of the pin!

rn1qk2r/ppp1ppb1/1n4p1/7p/3PP2P/2N1Bb2/P.text:
The doubled pawns aren't a problem...

...since we strengthen the center!

rnbq1rk1/pp2ppb1/6pp/2p5/3PP2P/2P2N2/P3B.text:
Black might get castled.

We'll castle as well.

rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/6p1/2p4p/4P2P/2P2N2/P2PB.text:
Black takes control over the d4-square.

We'll simply castle.

rnbqk2r/pp2ppb1/6pp/2p5/3PP2P/2P2N2/P4PP.text:
Black attacks the center in standard Grunfeld style.

We'll simply prepare to castle kingside.

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppb1/1n4p1/7p/3PP2P/2N2N2/PP.text:
Black fianchettoes.

We'll add support to the d4-pawn.

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppb1/6p1/7p/4P2P/2P2N2/P2P1P.text:
Black fianchettoes the dark-squared bishop.

The bishop moves so we can castle later. 

We use the flexibility of the English and don't commit to d4.

rnbqk2r/ppp1ppb1/6pp/8/4P2P/2P2N2/P2P1PP.text:
Black develops as expected.

We'll gain central control with our pawns.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/3n4/8/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
Black wants to fianchetto the bishop.

As mentioned in the previous study, we'll play h4 here! 

The idea is to attack Black's kingside pawn structure with h5 coming next.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/8/7P/2P2N2/P2PPPP1.text:
We'll recapture and avoid the queen trade. 

After Black's next decision (...h5/...h6/...Bg7) we are transposing to one of these lines.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/8/7P/2n2N2/PP1PPPP.text:
Yet another variation on the fifth move with the same statistic as 5...h6 (6%) is ...Nxc3. 

Black immediately trades the knights.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/1n4p1/7p/4P2P/2N2N2/PP1.text:
By retreating the knight, Black surrenders the center but is unable to generate enough pressure against it.

The second most popular move, with an occurrence of 12%.

We'll go ahead and grab the central squares!

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/6p1/3n3p/7P/1QN2N2/PP1P.text: 6. Qb3 is also a good option when 6...Nb6 could be met with 7. d4 or the direct 7. Ng5.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/6p1/3n3p/7P/2N2N2/PP1PP.text:
Black's response could be 5...h5, which happens 29% of the time. 

The idea is to completely block our h-pawn and stop the attack. The good news for us is that we have the g5-square for ourselves.

e4 is the most straightforward move. We gain space in the center with a tempo on Black's knight.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/6p1/7p/4P2P/2n2N2/PP1P1.text:
Black trades the knights, which happens a mind-blowing 79% of the time.

We recapture with the b-pawn. 

This is the most aggressive move, although 7. dxc3 was also
possible to offer a slightly better endgame.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/6pp/3n4/7P/2N2N2/PP1PPP.text:
Black goes for ...h6. The idea is that if we push h5, Black solidifies with ...g5. 

This happens nearly 25% of the time.

Let's just grab space in the center.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp2/6pp/8/4P2P/2n2N2/PP1P1P.text:
Black trades.

As usual, we have a stylistic choice of the more aggressive bxc3 or the endgame with dxc3.

Both options are good but I prefer to be more aggressive here.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3p4/2P5/2N5/PP1PPP.text:
Black goes for the Grunfeld approach.

We'll trade our flank pawn for Black's central pawn.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3n4/8/2N5/PP1PPPPP/R.text:
Black recaptures.

We'll develop the other knight to cover some central squares.

rnbqkb1r/pppppppp/5n2/8/2P5/8/PP1PPPPP/R.text:
Black responds with a minor piece development.

We'll develop the knight as well.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQK.text:
In the first study, we saw that our way of fighting the Grunfeld includes 5.h4. 

In this study, we'll cover Black's other fifth moves after 5.h4. 

Many times, Black's fifth move is an overreaction, so let's jump right in, beginning with 1.c4!

r1b1kb1r/pp2pppp/2n5/2p5/4P3/2P2N2/PPK2P.text:
But our king finds a safe square on c2. 

Definitely a better position for White.

Black's knight on c6 is nicely restricted by our c-pawn. 

We plan to develop the pieces (the bishops will go to c4 and e3) and gain space on the queenside with a4.

r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/n7/1N2p3/4P3/4B3/PP3PPP/.text:
And we bring the dark-squared bishop into the game. 

The light-squared bishop will be developed to c4, and our pieces will put pressure on the weak a7 and c7-squares, plus, we have the open c-file for our rook.

r1b1kb1r/pp3ppp/n7/1N2p3/4P3/8/PP3PPP/R1.text: Black defends against the fork on c7.
